lead: Thin films are layers from a few nanometres to a few micrometres thick, grown atom by atom or molecule by molecule on a surface. The method decides thickness control, sidewall coverage, uniformity and cost. Physical vapour deposition (PVD) turns a solid source into vapour that condenses. Chemical vapour deposition (CVD) reacts precursor gases on a heated substrate. Both appear in phone chips, solar cells, mirrors, cutting tools and packaging. Only a few universities teach these techniques in detail.
prereq: You need: 6.2 bottom-up synthesis for atom-by-atom growth, and Unit 4 electroplating for a wet coating comparison.

blocks.text: A film forms in four stages. A source supplies material. Transport carries it to the substrate. Deposition sticks it. Growth builds islands that join into a continuous layer. Vacuum is common: it gives vapour atoms a long mean free path, so they reach the wafer without colliding with air.

PVD is physical: a solid becomes vapour, then condenses. In thermal evaporation, a boat or crucible heats the source in vacuum; aluminium, gold and silver films are made this way. In sputtering, argon ions from a plasma bombard a target and knock out atoms. Sputtering gives better adhesion and can deposit alloys. PVD is line-of-sight: atoms travel straight, so sidewalls in a deep trench stay shadowed. It suits metals and simple oxides.
Substrate temperature is usually moderate, which helps plastic substrates. Film thickness is monitored by a quartz crystal microbalance. PVD does not require a surface chemical reaction.

CVD is chemical. Precursor gases enter a reactor, diffuse to the substrate, adsorb, react on the hot surface, and leave by-products that desorb. The film is the solid product. Thermal CVD needs a substrate often at several hundred degrees Celsius. Plasma-enhanced CVD (PECVD) uses a plasma to break precursor molecules, so the substrate can be cooler; it is common for silicon dioxide and silicon nitride.

Because gas reaches every exposed surface, CVD is conformal: it coats trench bottoms and sidewalls to nearly the same thickness. Precursors must be volatile, safe enough to handle, and react cleanly. Silane (SiH₄) with oxygen gives SiO₂; silane with ammonia gives Si₃N₄. Growth can be limited by gas transport or by surface reaction; the slower step controls rate.

Use PVD for metals, simple oxides, decorative and hard coatings, and mirrors. Use CVD for dielectric layers, semiconductor films, solar-cell coatings and uniform coverage of steps. PVD usually runs at lower substrate temperature and has no precursor chemistry. CVD is better for trenches but needs volatile precursors and often more heat or plasma.

Thickness in PVD is set by deposition rate × time. In CVD it is set by gas flow, pressure, temperature and time. Uniformity depends on wafer rotation and gas distribution. A hybrid choice is common: PVD for a metal contact, CVD for an insulating layer over it. Neither method is automatically better; the geometry and material decide. Adhesion improves after substrate cleaning.

examples.question: A copper film of thickness 100 nm is deposited on a 1.0 cm × 1.0 cm wafer. Density of copper = 8.9 g/cm³. Find the mass of copper deposited in g and μg.
steps: Thickness = 100 nm. Since 1 nm = 1×10⁻⁷ cm, thickness = 1.00×10⁻⁵ cm.
Volume = area × thickness = 1.0 cm² × 1.00×10⁻⁵ cm = 1.00×10⁻⁵ cm³.
Mass = density × volume = 8.9 g/cm³ × 1.00×10⁻⁵ cm³ = 8.9×10⁻⁵ g.
Convert: 1 g = 10⁶ μg, so mass = 8.9×10⁻⁵ × 10⁶ μg = 89 μg.
examples.answer: The mass is 8.9×10⁻⁵ g, equal to 89 μg.
examples.check:
area = 1.0 * 1.0
t = 100 * 1e-7
v = area * t
m = 8.9 * v
print(round(m, 12))
print(round(m * 1e6, 6))

traps: PVD is line-of-sight, so it may not coat deep sidewalls; CVD is conformal. Do not swap these.
Sputtering is physical, not a chemical reaction, even though a plasma is present.
Convert nm to cm carefully: 1 nm = 1×10⁻⁷ cm, not 10⁻⁹ cm.
Conformal means equal thickness on sidewalls and bottom; it does not mean single crystal.
CVD needs volatile precursors; a non-volatile solid cannot be fed as a gas.

quiz.a: PVD: solid source → vapour → film by condensation. CVD: precursor gases react on a heated substrate to form a solid film.
A coating of nearly equal thickness on flat surfaces, sidewalls and bottoms of features.
Vapour atoms travel in straight paths at low pressure; overhangs block them.

quiz.q: A 200 nm copper film is deposited on 2.0 cm². Density = 8.9 g/cm³. Find mass in μg.
A chip has a deep trench to fill with an insulator. Choose PVD or CVD and justify.
quiz.a: CVD. Gas reaches sidewalls and bottom, so the film is conformal; PVD shadows sidewalls.

quiz.q: Why can PECVD use a cooler substrate than thermal CVD?
quiz.a: The plasma supplies energy to break precursor bonds; the surface need not supply all activation energy as heat.

beyond: Not for the exam. Atomic layer deposition (ALD) is a cousin of CVD that splits the reaction into two self-limiting steps, giving one atomic layer per cycle. Industry uses cluster tools that combine PVD and CVD without air exposure. Search next for sputter deposition, PECVD silicon nitride and atomic layer deposition.
